## tidymodels (WIP)

additional tidymodels support is planned for daisugi. in particular, we're after the machines that are 'not-so-well-known', perform well, but are not included anywhere else, such as 'ebm' & 'ydf'. allowing ML engineers to swap out other boosters for Yggdrasil or Explainable boosting machines. 


</td><td width="42%" align="right"><img src="tidymodels.png" height="480"/></td></tr>
</table>


#### Prepare Dataset

following along with our getting started task, except with a tidymodels perspective, we have the forested data setup below.
```{r dataset}
library(daisugi)
library(forested)
library(parsnip)
library(rsample)
set.seed(5311)

# defining splits for training and testing datasets
splits <- rsample::initial_split(forested::forested)
training <- rsample::training(splits)
testing <- rsample::testing(splits)


# (x, y) Training:
x_train <- training |>
  # target (and factors as not all engines handle cats)
  dplyr::select(-forested, -tree_no_tree, -land_type, -county)

# our target variable:
y_train <- training |> dplyr::select(forested) |> dplyr::pull()

# (x, y) Testing:
x_test <- testing |>
  dplyr::select(-forested, -tree_no_tree, -land_type, -county)

y_test <- testing |> dplyr::select(forested) |> dplyr::pull()

head(y_test)
```


### EBMs

The Explainable Boosting Machine is registered as a `boost_tree`, it has a few similar parameters, and many unique ones. a handful of the unique parameters were also registered to dials within daisugi so full-on-total hyperparameter optimization can be done within cross-validation in tidymodels.

check out the registered & tunable parameters. 
```{r}
ebm_cls_spec <-
  boost_tree(
    # GBM parameters
    trees = 500,
    min_n = 2,
    tree_depth = 5,
    learn_rate = 0.015,
    stop_iter = 250
  ) |>
  set_mode("classification") |>
  set_engine(
    "ebm",
    # tier 1 ebm parameters
    num_interactions = 3L,
    max_bins = 1024L,
    greedy_ratio = 10L,
    smoothing_rounds = 75L,
    regularization_lambda = 0L,
    regularization_alpha = 0L,
    # tier 2 ebm parameters
    max_interaction_bins = 64L,
    interaction_smoothing_rounds = 75L,
    outer_bags = 14L,
    inner_bags = 0L
  )

ebm_cls_spec
```



```{r fit}
# fit --
ebm_cls_fit <- ebm_cls_spec |>
  fit(
    forested ~ .,
    data = training |> dplyr::select(-tree_no_tree, -land_type, -county)
  )

# predictions --
preds <- predict(ebm_cls_fit, x_test, type = "raw")
preds
```
